title.title: Title
title.about: The report's title as its cover prints it.

subtitle.title: Subtitle
subtitle.about: The line under the title, when the cover has one.
subtitle.note: Empty when the PDF prints none.

type.title: Type
type.about: The kind of work this is.
type.note: Crossref files every Openscholar Report as a report. Zenodo and Openscholar use the type chosen here.

language.title: Language
language.about: The language the report is written in.

date.title: Date published
date.about: When the report was published: a year, a month or a day, as precisely as the PDF states it, and today at the latest.
date.note: Crossref keeps it as precise as it is. Zenodo takes a whole date, so a year or a month goes there as its first day. A PDF that states no date gets today.

licence.title: License
licence.about: Every Openscholar Report is published under CC BY 4.0, as the agreement you signed says.

authors.title: Authors
authors.about: Everyone the report credits, in the order its citation lists them.
authors.note: The PDF's authors are filled in. Add editors, translators and others here, and set their role.

name.title: Name
name.about: The name as the report prints it. An organization's full name works too.
name.note: A person's name reaches Crossref and Zenodo as family name, then given names: the last word is taken as the family name. An organization's name, one with a word such as Department, Ministry or University in it, is sent whole.

kind.title: Role
kind.about: What this person is to the report. Most people are authors.
kind.note: Only authors are named in the report's citation. Everyone else is listed with their role under Contributions on the report's page, and Crossref and Zenodo get each person's role.

orcid.title: ORCID iD
orcid.about: A free number that tells researchers with the same name apart.
orcid.note: When the PDF prints none, ORCID is searched for one person with exactly this name at one of these institutions.

affiliations.title: Affiliations
affiliations.about: Where this person worked when the report was written.
affiliations.note: An institution with a ROR ID is sent with it, so Crossref and Zenodo know which one it is. One typed by hand goes as a name alone.

contributions.title: Contributions
contributions.about: What this person did for the work, in the 14 roles of CRediT.
contributions.note: Filled in only when the PDF has a contributions statement. Leaving it empty is fine.

corresponding.title: Corresponding author
corresponding.about: The person readers write to about the report.
corresponding.note: Switched on only when the PDF marks one.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.about: The abstract or summary your PDF prints, copied as it is.
abstract.note: When the PDF prints neither, Write from the PDF drafts one for you to check and change.

topics.title: Topics
topics.about: What the report is about, in OpenAlex's topics.
topics.note: OpenAlex's classifier reads the title and abstract. The bar on a topic shows how sure it was. Topics you add have none.

keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.about: Your own words for what the report is about.
keywords.note: The PDF's keywords. When it lists none, up to five from OpenAlex's classifier.

sdgs.title: Sustainable Development Goals
sdgs.about: The UN goals the report is substantially about.
sdgs.note: At most three are filled in. Add or remove any.

design.title: Study design
design.note: Filled in only when the PDF makes it clear. Zenodo shows it as a methods note.

places.title: Places studied
places.about: The countries and regions the report is about, not where its authors work.

funding.title: Funding
funding.about: Who paid for the work, with the grant numbers as printed.
funding.note: Funders are looked up on OpenAlex and ROR. One found there goes with its ROR ID, and with its Funder Registry ID where it has one. One typed by hand goes as a name alone.

references.title: References
references.about: The works this report cites, as its reference list writes them.
references.note: Paste the list, or upload it as a BibTeX, RIS or plain text file. Every DOI the PDF prints is filled in, and Crossref links each reference with a DOI to the work it cites.

links.title: Data, code and versions
links.about: Where the report's data, code, other versions and supplements live.
links.note: Each is a web address or a DOI.

agreement.title: The publishing agreement
agreement.about: What you and Openscholar agree to before your report is published.
agreement.note: You keep the copyright. Ticking the box agrees for you and every co-author, so check they have agreed first. A signed agreement can't be changed.

doi.title: DOI
doi.about: A permanent link to your report that keeps working wherever its page moves.
doi.note: It's reserved when you sign, so you can print it in your PDF. It works once your report goes live.

byline.title: The series line
byline.about: The line every report in this series prints, naming the series, its ISSN and the report's DOI.
byline.note: It has to be text in the PDF, not a picture, because the checks look for it. Choose Add it for me and Openscholar adds a last page with the line.

checks.title: Checks
checks.about: What Openscholar checks before a report can go live, such as the series line in the PDF and whether the work is already published.
checks.note: Each check says what it looked for, and what to fix when it fails. If you're sure a check is wrong, ask for a person to review it.

issn.title: ISSN
issn.about: The number that identifies the series, as a journal's does.
issn.note: Pending until the series is registered. Your report's DOI works without it.

activation.title: Activating
activation.about: Activating makes your report public: its page opens, its DOI starts working, and it's registered.
activation.note: An activation comes from your workspace's balance, or is paid for here. A voucher code takes money off its price.
